title: TSMC to invest up to $1 billion in Anthropic, OpenAI
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

TSMC’s decision to invest up to $500 million in Anthropic marks a significant step toward closer financial ties between semiconductor manufacturing and artificial intelligence development. On November 10, 2026, the Taiwanese chipmaker’s board approved buying Anthropic common shares at the company’s initial public offering price. It separately authorized up to $500 million for OpenAI preferred stock, spreading its exposure across two prominent AI developers.

The strategic logic is straightforward. AI developers need enormous computing resources to train models and serve customers. That demand supports spending on advanced chips, making their commercial success relevant to the manufacturers behind the hardware. Reuters describes TSMC’s move as positioning the company to benefit both from supplying AI infrastructure and from owning stakes in influential developers.

For Anthropic, the investment can be read as a vote of confidence from a company whose manufacturing decisions underpin the broader AI industry. However, financial backing should not be confused with a guaranteed supply agreement. TSMC’s announcement specifies the proposed share purchase but does not disclose preferential manufacturing access, exclusive arrangements, or commitments to provide particular chips.

The potential benefits also come with risks. Taking an equity stake adds exposure to Anthropic’s valuation and business performance alongside TSMC’s existing exposure to demand for AI hardware. If adoption disappoints or infrastructure spending slows, those exposures could reinforce each other. Conversely, sustained growth could generate investment returns while supporting demand throughout the semiconductor supply chain.

Ultimately, the announcement suggests TSMC sees value in participating more directly in the businesses driving computing demand. The key distinction is between authorization and execution: the board has approved an investment ceiling, rather than announced a completed $500 million purchase. Its eventual significance will depend on the transaction’s completion, Anthropic’s performance, and whether AI spending produces durable commercial returns over the coming years for customers and investors alike.

TSMC Board of Directors Meeting Resolutions

HSINCHU, Taiwan, R.O.C., Nov. 10, 2026 – The TSMC (TWSE: 2330, NYSE: TSM) Board of
Directors today held a meeting, which passed the following resolutions:

1. Approved the 2026 third quarter Business Report and Financial Statements. Third quarter
consolidated revenue was NT$1,494.24 billion and net income was NT$763.06 billion, with
diluted earnings per share of NT$29.43.

2. Approved the distribution of a NT$9.0 per share cash dividend for the third quarter of 2026, and
set March 17, 2027 as the record date for common stock shareholders entitled to participate in
this cash dividend distribution, and the ex-dividend date for the common shares shall be March
11, 2027. As required by Article 165 of Taiwan’s Company Law, the shareholders’ register shall
be closed for five days prior to the record date (March 13 through March 17, 2027) for
registration transfer, and the dividend will be paid on April 8, 2027. The ex-dividend date and
the record date for entitlement to participate in this cash dividend distribution for TSMC
American Depositary Shares (ADSs) will be March 11, 2027.

3. To meet long-term capacity plans based on market demand forecasts and TSMC’s technology
development roadmap, the Board approved capital appropriations of approximately
US$40,926.70 million for purposes mainly including: (1) Installation and upgrade of advanced
technology capacity; (2) Installation and upgrade of advanced packaging, mature and/or
specialty technology capacity; (3) Fab construction, and installation of fab facility systems; (4)
2027 R&D capital investments, sustaining capital expenditures, and capitalized leased assets.

4. Approved the investment of no more than US$500 million in the establishment of an investment
company for the purpose of making strategic investments in the semiconductor industry and
related ecosystem.

5. Approved the investments in (1) Anthropic, PBC at its per share initial public offering price in
an amount not to exceed US$500 million to acquire Anthropic’s common shares; and (2) OpenAI
Group PBC in an amount not to exceed US$500 million to acquire OpenAI’s preferred stock.

About TSMC
TSMC pioneered the pure-play foundry business model when it was founded in 1987 and has been
the world’s leading dedicated semiconductor foundry ever since. The Company supports a thriving
ecosystem of global customers and partners with the industry’s leading process technologies and
portfolio of design enablement solutions to unleash innovation for the global semiconductor industry.
With global operations spanning Asia, Europe, and North America, TSMC serves as a committed
corporate citizen around the world.

TSMC deployed 305 distinct process technologies, and manufactured 12,682 products for 534
customers in 2025 by providing the broadest range of advanced, specialty and advanced packaging
technology services. The Company is headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan. For more information please
visit https://www.tsmc.com.
